text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Among 25 political organisations which presented their lists for the October 20 parliament elections, only six could pay the 12,000 litas security required by law from their own funds.

- Klaipeda businessman Vidmantas Bukauskas, who was kidnapped last week, was released Sunday night but refused to give evidence or start legal procedings against the kidnappers. It is thought the criminals released Bukauskas after a $100,000 ransom was paid.

- A statistics department report showed that the average salary in Lithuania in August was $168.61 in Lithuania, $203.08 in Latvia and $223.79 in Estonia. The minimum salary was the lowest in Lithuania $52.5, $55.68 in Estonia and $68.84 in Latvia.

- The authorities of Butinges Nafta signed a letter of intent with German Preussag Anlagenbau and U.S. group Fluor to construct the Butinge oil terminal. Both companies suggested full financing of the construction works. If the government and parliament provide guarantees, the financial side of Butinge terminal construction will be settled, Butinge officials say.
- The troubled Lithuanian State Commercial Bank registered new 165 million litas share emission in the securities commission on Monday. The whole new share capital will be bought by the state.

- Lithuanian prosecutors presented on Monday charges against the suspected leader of the criminal group the Vilnius Brigade, Igor Tiomkin, who was extradited from Germany and delivered to Lukiskiu prison in Vilnius last week.

- The director of Lietuvos Energija said Monday that the prices of heating energy (8.94 cents per kilowatt hour) will not change until Christmas despite the fact that the price is 22 percent lower than the cost price and the request of the World Bank to raise the price.

- Lithuanian diplomats submitted additional answers to the European Commission questionnaire. According to the answers, the EU will decide about the readiness of Lithuania for European Union membership.
- The center of information about registered real estate in Lithuania and whether it has been mortgaged will start functioning in 1997.

- South Korean company Jinro Group subsidiary based in Hong Kong Jinro H.K. International Limited transferred to the Bank of Lithuania 11.6 million litas for 67.2 percent the small Senamiescio Bankas. Before registering, the Bank of Lithuania will verify the origin of the capital.
